transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Gonzalez (StratusHealth CTO), Ethan Park (VP Eng), Lina Morales (DevOps), Samir Khan (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Okay, great everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. We'll run through the model catalog and some benchmarks and then talk about what a POC would look like. How's the audio?
[00:10] Marta: Sounds good, Jordan, thanks. We have about 45 minutes. want to focus first on which open models are a good fit for our doc summarization workload, and then touch on triage/chatbot latency.
[00:20] Jordan: Perfect. Priya, I'll hand over to you for the walkthrough.
[00:24] Priya: Thanks. Hi team. So the Redwood model catalog is a curated list of open models we've validated across our runtime. For each model we show a compatibility matrix \u2014 like what quantization profiles are supported (FP16, int8, int4), whether KV cache streaming works, maximum effective sequence length, and which hardware we recommend (T4, A10, A100, H100).
[00:40] Priya: I'll share my screen \u2014 here's the catalog sheet. You can see model families (Llama2, Mistral, Falcon, Orca variants), then our per-model profile: throughput tokens/sec, median generation latency at 512 tokens, and recommended quantization for production.
[00:55] Ethan: Quick question \u2014 when you say "recommended quantization", is that purely cost-driven or does it include QA/regression checks on output quality?
[01:05] Priya: Good question. It's a balance \u2014 we run a suite of evals (ROUGE/BLEU style for summarization, and custom prompt sets for your use cases) and compare quality deltas. For many summarization workloads, int8 with per-channel quantization gives 10-20x speedup with <2% drop in ROUGE. We flag models where quality regressions are larger.
[01:25] Marta: Can you show an example benchmark for, say, Mistral-7B vs Llama2-70B? We're trying to weigh smaller optimized models versus large ones with distillation.
[01:35] Priya: Sure. On H100 we see Mistral-7B (int8) at ~1,200 tokens/sec with median per-token latency ~6ms when batching is enabled; Llama2-70B (FP16) is ~350 tokens/sec with ~18ms per-token in our default profile. But quality depends on context length and prompt engineering \u2014 for long-form summarization Llama2-70B still has an edge on abstractive quality in our eval set.
[01:55] Lina: Those numbers assume batching, right? For chat/triage where latency budget is tight, what do you recommend?
[02:05] Priya: Yes batching improves throughput. For low-latency inference (sub-100ms response) we recommend smaller models on Dedicated H100 or even TPU-like configs, plus prefix caching for repeated prompts. We also have streaming enabled so you can start rendering tokens immediately. The catalog marks streaming-capable models and whether they support function/tool calling.
[02:30] Jordan: I'll interject \u2014 for StratusHealth's triage bot you mentioned 500ms SLO for first response; we usually recommend a two-model strategy: a small fast model for immediate triage and a larger model for final summary generation asynchronously. This keeps UX snappy and controls cost.
[02:50] Ethan: What's the typical price delta between hosted small model and dedicated H100? Ballpark figures fine.
[02:58] Jordan: Ballpark: hosted for a smaller int8 model might be $X per 1M tokens (Jordan: note, we'll send exact pricing), Dedicated H100 amortized can be cheaper per-token at scale but requires commit. We'll include unit economics in the deck.
[03:12] Marta: Security \u2014 we need to understand data residency and KMS options. If we go private on-prem, can Redwood integrate with our HSM?
[03:22] Priya: Yes. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and provide audit logs, RBAC, SSO. The compatibility matrix includes which deployment modes each model is validated on \u2014 hosted, dedicated, private. Some of our open model variants have additional licensing notes which we surface.
[03:40] Samir: On that licensing note, do you have any automated checks for model license compliance in the catalog?
[03:47] Priya: We surface license metadata per model and flag any models with restrictive terms. We don't replace legal review but we make the metadata easily searchable.
[03:55] Jordan: Back to benchmarks \u2014 Priya is going to talk through the benchmark methodology so you can interpret numbers.
[04:00] Priya: Right. We run both microbenchmarks (latency/throughput across sequence lengths and batch sizes) and application-level evals using your prompt sets. For summarization we run a 200-sample set with 1k-3k token inputs to measure coherence and hallucination rates; for chat triage we run latency p95 and p99 plus cold-start numbers. We also test cache hit rates with simulated repeated prompts.
[04:25] Ethan: When you ran the repo benchmarks, were they single-node or multi-node? We expect some of our production traffic to be parallel requests across many users.
[04:33] Priya: Both. The sheet has single-node numbers and scaling curves for multi-node configs. Typically you see linear scaling up to the saturating point where IO or KV cache synchronization kicks in. We also annotate where sequence length changes kernel selection \u2014 that affects latency.
[04:50] Marta: Can you walk me through a compatibility matrix row? I want to know what the fields are.
[04:55] Priya: Sure. For each model we include: family/name, recommended quantizations, supported sequence length, streaming (yes/no), function-calling (yes/no), recommended hardware, observed median latency @ 512 tokens, throughput tokens/sec @ recommended batch, and production notes (e.g., "requires int8 calibration for best perf").
[05:20] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[05:24] Priya: Also we include the "fallthrough" variants \u2014 smaller distilled versions or quantized snapshots we fallback to when capacity is constrained; that's part of Redwood's smart routing. So your app can declare latency SLO and we can route to a compatible variant to maintain availability.
[05:40] Ethan: For private deployments, how do you handle model updates and rollouts? We need strict version pinning and audit history.
[05:48] Priya: We support pinned model versions and rollouts with canary and A/B. The console shows per-version metrics and you can configure automatic rollback on quality regressions. We tie evals to prompt sets and can gate rollouts if regressions exceed threshold.
[06:05] Marta: Ok, demo time \u2014 can you show a quick end-to-end: pick a model, run a sample summarization and show output + latency metrics?
[06:12] Priya: Yep. I'm running a live inference on Mistral-7B int8 in Hosted for demo. Sending a 1.2k token clinical note...
[06:30] [06:30] Priya: Output streaming now \u2014 you can see tokens appearing. Latency to first token: ~120ms. Total generation time: 1.1s. Here's the summary \u2014 (reads) "Patient presents with chest pain..."
[06:45] Marta: Looks concise. How does hallucination look in these shorter summaries?
[06:48] Priya: For structured clinical notes we see low hallucination if prompts are constrained. We run hallucination checks in the eval harness and flag model+prompt combos with higher rates.
[07:00] Ethan: Could you re-run with Llama2-70B for comparison? Just one sample.
[07:05] Priya: I can but on Hosted it will be slower to spin up; but here's a previously captured run \u2014 latency first token ~220ms, full gen 3.9s, and quality score +3 points on our abstractive metrics versus Mistral on that example.
[07:25] Jordan: Note that those historical runs are in bench-metrics.csv \u2014 we'll send that.
[07:30] Lina: For our ops team, what's in the compatibility matrix about memory footprint per model? We operate constrained GPUs in some sites.
[07:38] Priya: We list peak VRAM at common batch sizes and sequence lengths for each model variant. Also recommended quantization reduces footprint; int8 snapshots often halve memory usage. For very constrained devices we suggest distilled families or running with smaller sequence windows.
[07:56] Marta: Any gotchas with prefix/KV cache when using long context summarization? We rely on 8k+ context windows sometimes.
[08:04] Priya: For long contexts we recommend models with optimized attention kernels and we select kernels per hardware. Our catalog calls out models that have efficient attention implementations and ones where beyond 4k you start to see quadratic slowdowns. We also support sliding-window and chunked encoding patterns in the SDK.
[08:25] Ethan: Can platform routing automatically fallback to a compatible variant if H100 capacity is saturated?
[08:32] Priya: Yes \u2014 smart routing can fallback by policy. For example you set a latency SLO and cost tier; Redwood will route to a smaller quantized variant if the primary model isn't available. The compatibility matrix includes a list of "compatible fallback candidates".
[08:50] Jordan: We're circling back to POC scope \u2014 the ask was: run your production prompts against 3 candidate models (Mistral-7B int8, Llama2-70B FP16, and a distilled 13B). Measure p50/p95 latency and quality metrics and give cost estimates. Priya, is that doable in a week?
[09:06] Priya: Yes \u2014 if StratusHealth provides anonymized samples and traffic profile we can run a 1-week POC on Dedicated H100 and give you a report. We'll capture cold-starts, warm cache, and scaling behavior.
[09:18] Samir: On security for a Dedicated deployment \u2014 we need to ensure logs don't contain PHI. Does Redwood support redaction or tokenization before logs are persisted?
[09:27] Priya: We support configurable log redaction and can disable transcript capture. For POC we can run with redaction enabled and send aggregated metrics only. Also, integrations with customer KMS mean model keys and tokens are under your control.
[09:42] Marta: Good. On licensing again \u2014 any open models you wouldn't recommend for production due to license?
[09:48] Priya: We surface license risk, and if a model has a non-commercial clause or unclear terms we mark it as "requires legal review". We avoid recommending those for enterprise production.
[09:58] Ethan: What about running your bench on our on-prem infra? We have an on-prem GPU cluster with A100s.
[10:04] Priya: We can run the POC on your infra via Private deployment. That takes a bit longer for onboarding (networking, KMS) \u2014 typical timeline a few weeks \u2014 but for benchmarking we can also run a short-sprint remote bench on our Dedicated capacity and then replicate to your infra later.
[10:20] Jordan: Let's talk artifacts \u2014 we'll send the model-catalog.xlsx, bench-metrics.csv, and a compat-matrix.pdf. Any preferences for the sample prompts format?
[10:29] Ethan: CSV with input_id, input_text, expected_output (optional) works best. We'll strip PHI.
[10:34] Jordan: Perfect.
[10:36] [10:36] Priya: Small demo note: streaming and function calling \u2014 we flagged which models support structured outputs and function hooks. For integration with your triage microservice we recommend models that support function-calling to produce JSON fields (symptom, severity, recommended action). That reduces post-processing.
[10:55] Marta: Is function calling supported across quantized variants?
[10:59] Priya: Mostly yes, but we test to be sure. The compatibility matrix shows function-calling support by variant. Sometimes lower-quality quantization can break deterministic tokenization for JSON outputs so we call that out.
[11:15] Ethan: Do you have examples of cost optimization knobs we can tweak after POC?
[11:20] Jordan: Yes \u2014 batching, cache TTL, two-model pipelines, async post-processing, and routing policies. Redwood Optimize will surface suggestions based on actual traffic.
[11:30] Lina: For cost predictions, do you provide per-route per-model cost breakdowns?
[11:34] Priya: Console shows token-level cost breakdowns per route and per model and historical trends; we can export those to CSV for finance.
[11:45] Marta: Ok, last bits \u2014 schedule follow-up and assign owners.
[11:50] Jordan: Action items we captured: we'll send the artifacts and Priya will run the POC if you provide samples. Proposed follow-up 2026-07-28 to review results.
[12:00] Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:05] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the files. Bye.
